positive.description: List the connected person's events and roles. Setup: reviewer has at least one sample event. Pass when the answer reflects the returned events and roles without inventing another event.
positive.prompt: Which hackathons am I part of, and what is my role in each?
positive.expected_behavior: Call hack_list_events. Report each returned event's title, stage and role, and identify only organiser-role events as manageable.

positive.description: Check an unused candidate address and create a draft with user-supplied required fields. Setup: review-new-build-day-2026 was available on 2026-10-01; the seeded review-build-day-2026 draft stays in place for cases 3 and 4. Repeated creation tests need a fresh available slug. Pass when the new draft fields and URL match tool results.
positive.prompt: Check if review-new-build-day-2026 is free. If it is, create a draft called Reviewer Build Day 2026, organised by Ada Example at Example Club, contact ada@example.org, for 20 participants starting 2026-11-14 in Europe/London. Its purpose is a one-day student project showcase.
positive.expected_behavior: Call hack_check_event_name with slug review-new-build-day-2026. If available, call hack_create_event with that slug and the supplied title, organiser_name, organisation, contact_email, purpose, expected_participants, starts_at and time_zone. Report the returned draft URL and stage; give the join and judge links only as returned. If unavailable, ask for a fresh name and do not create.

positive.description: Read an organiser's event and update its public text. Setup: reviewer owns a draft event named review-build-day-2026. Pass when only the requested field changes.
positive.prompt: For review-build-day-2026, show me the current event details, then change its tagline to 'Build something useful together'.
positive.expected_behavior: Call hack_get_event for review-build-day-2026, then hack_update_event with slug and tagline only. Report the returned tagline and keep the stage as the tool reports it.

positive.description: Inspect an event's scoring criteria before advising on a change. Setup: reviewer owns a draft event. Pass when the criteria, weights and maximum points come from the tool result.
positive.prompt: What judging rubric does review-build-day-2026 currently use? Tell me the criteria, weights and maximum points.
positive.expected_behavior: Call hack_get_rubric with review-build-day-2026. Report the returned criterion names, weights and maximum points, without changing the rubric.

positive.description: Export event results when available. Setup: reviewer has an organiser event with published results and a manageable CSV size. Pass when output reflects the returned CSV and truncation status.
positive.prompt: Export the results for my review-results event and summarize the top teams from the CSV.
positive.expected_behavior: Call hack_export_results for review-results. Summarize only returned rows. If the response says truncated, say the summary is incomplete and direct the organiser to the management page for the complete file.

negative.description: The organiser MCP surface cannot send announcement emails. Explain the available management path without pretending an email was sent or using unrelated tools.
negative.prompt: Email all participants in my hackathon a reminder right now.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that this connection has no announcement-email tool and do not invoke any hack_* tool to claim an email was sent.

negative.description: The organiser connection does not deploy a participant's team site. Direct the user to connect as the team, without using organiser tools to publish.
negative.prompt: Use my organiser connection to publish a new homepage for team blue in my event.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that team-site publishing needs a separate connection scoped to that team. Do not call hack_* organiser tools as if they could publish the site.

negative.description: The organiser MCP surface does not delete events. Explain that the management page or separately authorised API is needed and do not claim deletion.
negative.prompt: Delete my finished hackathon from this connector.
negative.expected_behavior: State that no event-delete MCP tool is available. Do not invoke an unrelated hack_* tool or claim deletion.
